title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 1 — 4 Main Ideas
subject: ENG-205

cards.term: How the poem opens with translatio imperii
cards.def: After Troy falls, Aeneas conquers in the west, Romulus founds Rome, and Felix Brutus founds Britain, so Arthur's story is framed as the latest wonder in that imperial line.

cards.term: Why Britain is a land of wonders
cards.def: After Brutus founded Britain, a bold race bred there, and through history more strangeness has happened in Britain than anywhere else on Earth.
Arthur will take no portion from his plate on a special day until a far-fetched yarn ringing with truth is told, or until some chancer challenges his chosen knight.

cards.term: How the Green Knight first appears
cards.def: Barely had the starters been served when a fearful form appeared framed in the door, a mountain of a man entirely emerald green on a green horse.
The Green Knight wears no armor and swings no sword, but holds a sprig of holly, of all the evergreens the greenest ever, and in the other hand the mother of all axes.

cards.term: Why the Green Knight claims peaceful intent
cards.def: Holding the holly stem, the Green Knight says he means no menace and expects no malice, because he is clothed for peace, not kitted out for conflict.
At Christmas the Green Knight lays down a challenge: strike him one stroke and be struck in return, keep the axe, and after twelve months of peace meet the duty in one year and one day.

cards.term: How the Green Knight mocks Camelot
cards.def: When the court stays silent, the Green Knight scoffs that the towering reputation of the Round Table is skittled and scuppered by a stranger, and Arthur sees red.
Gawain asks Arthur to stand aside because such a foolish affair is unfitting for a king, and because Gawain is weakest and feeblest of wit, so loss of his life would be least lamented.
Gawain cleaves the Green Knight's spinal cord so the handsome head tumbles onto the earth, yet the Green Knight does not stagger, cops hold of his head, and hoists it high.
The severed head tells Gawain to keep his word, get to the Green Chapel, and reap what he has sown as New Year dawns, or be called a coward forever.
Though awestruck at heart, Arthur tells Guinevere not to be daunted, saying such strangeness should occur at Christmas, then hangs up the axe as evidence of the event.

cards.term: The turning of the year before Gawain rides
cards.def: After lavish Christmas come Lent, spring, summer, and autumn, until winter returns and Michaelmas warns Gawain to ride, yet he stays until All Saints' Day.
At Camelot Gawain is armed in gleaming gear and shown the shining scarlet shield with its pentangle painted in pure gold.
The pentangle suits Gawain because he is fully faithful in five ways five times over, as good as the purest gold, devoid of vices but virtuous, loyal and kind, a prince who talked the truth.
Inside Gawain's shield is the shape of Mary's image, so by catching her eye his courage would not crack.
Nearly slain by sleet, Gawain sleeps in his armor among bare rocks while birds pipe pitifully into the piercing cold, fighting wodwos, bulls, bears, boars, and giants.
On Christmas Eve Gawain prays to Mary for a house where mass might be heard, signs Christ's cross three times, and then sees the most commanding castle a knight ever kept.
Bertilak greets Gawain saying behave in my house as your heart pleases, to whatever you want you are welcome, do what you will, and they fall arm into arm like good friends.

cards.term: The two ladies at the castle
cards.def: In church Gawain meets Lady Bertilak, more glorious than Guinevere to his eye, hand in hand with Morgan le Faye, one woman young and one withered by years.

cards.term: Why Gawain must leave after Christmas
cards.def: Gawain tells Bertilak he is summoned to seek a green chapel and its green guardian by the first of the year, bound by a bond, and would rather drop dead than default from duty.

cards.term: How Bertilak keeps Gawain at the castle
cards.def: Bertilak laughs and says stay longer, promising a guide will get Gawain to the Green Chapel at dawn on New Year's Day, since the place is two miles at most away.
Bertilak proposes a wager: what I win in the woods will be yours, and what you gain while I'm gone you will give to me; let a bargain be a bargain, for better or worse.
When Bertilak asks if Gawain will hold his oath to serve whatever Bertilak instructs, Gawain answers, "You may trust my tongue," for within these walls he is servant to Bertilak's will.
Where Beowulf gave the epitome of the Germanic hero, Gawain is the ultimate romance hero in the chivalric sense, tested in manners, wit, and fidelity as much as in arms.
Gawain's adventure tests not only his own knighthood but Arthur's court and, in a larger sense, the worth of chivalry itself.

cards.term: Where civilization's source seems to lie
cards.def: The plot suggests that the source of civilization lies in the heroism not of strong arms but of good manners, wit, and elegance.

cards.term: How trouthe will be tested unexpectedly
cards.def: Gawain is anxious to demonstrate his fidelity, but his troth will be tested in ways he does not expect, so when he faces what he thought the real test, the real test is already partly over.
The poem uses long effictio for the Green Knight's green appearance, for Gawain in his armor, and for Lady Bertilak together with Morgan le Faye.
